records.matter: Protected disclosure outside the local chain of command followed by threatened rating and assignment consequences
records.qualification_basis: An FBI technician assigned temporary duty reported a compliance concern to a Special Agent in Charge authorized to receive it.

source_packets.supports: OIG found reasonable grounds for reprisal after a protected disclosure outside the technician’s home-office chain of command; a supervisor threatened a lower appraisal and denial of future temporary-duty opportunities.
The investigative summary records the reprisal finding and corrective-action referral.

records.source_supports: A protected technical disclosure was treated as an improper chain-of-command bypass and followed by threatened professional consequences.
source_does_not_establish: a final OARM merits disposition
the complete evidence underlying the technical concern
whether every manager shared the same rationale
a complete continuous K0 chain without field adjudication

records.matter: Protected disclosure followed by two non-selections and supervisory intervention in recommendations
records.qualification_basis: An FBI analyst made protected disclosures and later sought two positions governed by supervisory recommendations and selection gates.

source_packets.supports: OIG reported reasonable grounds to believe an FBI analyst suffered reprisal after protected disclosures.
The underlying misconduct report documents the non-selection and supervisory conduct reviewed by OIG.

records.source_supports: Official oversight found reasonable grounds to believe protected disclosures contributed to adverse non-selection actions.
source_does_not_establish: a final OARM merits disposition
that the analyst was the objectively best candidate
a complete explanation-before and explanation-after mutation
a complete continuous K0 chain without field adjudication

records.matter: Congressional testimony followed by loose-cannon and chain-of-command framing, teaching exclusion, proposed discipline, and later suspension
records.qualification_basis: Neil Jacobs was an Assistant District Director for Investigations with direct operational knowledge of fraud-referral practices.

source_packets.supports: The report records Jacobs’s congressional testimony, an attempt to end his teaching role, the “loose cannon” and “circumvented the chain of command” characterization, proposed discipline for reckless disregard of truth, and an OSC-sustained retaliation claim.

records.source_supports: The official record contains a bounded professional contradiction, explicit standing and loyalty reclassification, multiple gate actions, and later oversight findings.
source_does_not_establish: identical motive for every INS actor
that every later suspension charge lacked independent merit
a timely independent stay before all consequences
a complete continuous K0 chain without field adjudication

records.matter: Situated operational warning met with “just a clerk” and loyalty framing but no substantiated adverse personnel action
records.qualification_basis: Kathy Bell processed fingerprint cards and criminal-history reports and supplied information later corroborated in material respects.

source_packets.supports: The report records that managers called Bell “just a clerk,” implied she did not understand the procedures, and viewed her as disloyal, but found no adverse personnel action or prohibited practice caused by her disclosures.

records.source_supports: Reclassification language can exist without a completed material gate consequence, providing a direct non-event comparator.
source_does_not_establish: a substantiated retaliation action
feedback-source removal
blocked correction or exit
a ceiling-conversion event

records.matter: Contractor chain-of-command policy inconsistent with statutory whistleblower protections
records.institution: U.S. Marshals Service contractor and contract-management system

source_packets.supports: OIG did not substantiate the individual reprisal complaint but found the contractor policy and contract terms inconsistent with statutory whistleblower protections and capable of chilling disclosures.

records.source_supports: A defective or chilling chain-of-command policy is not automatically a substantiated bounded K0 event.
source_does_not_establish: individual reprisal in the investigated matter
a qualified contradiction followed by proven reclassification
a completed material consequence caused by the policy
a ceiling-conversion event

records.matter: Merits standard for lawful discipline labeled insubordination

source_packets.supports: MSPB explains that a misconduct label must be proved and defines insubordination as willful and intentional refusal to obey an authorized order the superior is entitled to have obeyed.
MSPB describes independent appeal routes for removals, suspensions, reductions, and whistleblower claims.

records.source_supports: Professional disagreement does not immunize refusal of a lawful authorized order; the burden remains on the agency to prove the charged elements.
source_does_not_establish: that every insubordination charge is valid
that every disciplined employee receives a stay
a K0 event
observed effectiveness in every appeal

records.matter: Independent stay halting a whistleblower removal while corrective-action litigation proceeds
records.institution: U.S. Office of Special Counsel / Merit Systems Protection Board

source_packets.supports: OSC reported an indefinite MSPB stay halting removal after finding strong evidence of retaliation and filing a corrective-action complaint.
MSPB initially granted a 45-day stay based on reasonable grounds to believe protected disclosures contributed to termination.

records.source_supports: A structurally independent body can preserve standing and suspend an employment gate before final merits resolution.
source_does_not_establish: a final merits decision
complete restoration or compensation
that every whistleblower can obtain a stay
observed prevention of every K0 event

records.matter: Anti-gag enforcement rescinding chain-of-command restrictions and a reprimand
records.institution: U.S. Office of Special Counsel and affected federal agencies

source_packets.supports: OSC reported withdrawal or revision of policies forcing all issues through the chain of command and rescission of a VA reprimand that improperly sanctioned an employee for not using official channels.

records.source_supports: Independent enforcement can remove a chilling rule and correct a formal personnel record without treating policy existence as observed universal protection.
source_does_not_establish: that retaliation never occurred
a pre-action stay in every matter
universal compliance after correction
a completed K0 event
